provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. The colour roles are constants: background is palette[0], the figure is palette[4] and the marker is palette[6]. Steps: (1) Erase the marker cells to background. (2) Find the marker's junction, which is the cell with the most 4-neighbours inside the marker. (3) Measure the arm length in each of the four directions from the junction. The long arm is the unique arm of length 2: the T stem, or the 2-cell arm of the asymmetric cross. (4) The constructor defines the mirror direction as the long arm rotated 90 degrees CCW in image coordinates, (dy,dx)->(-dx,dy). Rotations (d4<4) keep this relation. Reflections (d4>=4) invert its handedness, so for those the program uses the CW rotation (dy,dx)->(dx,-dy). (5) Take the tight bounding box of the figure-colour cells and reflect it across the axis perpendicular to the mirror direction. Stamp its figure cells flush against the box on the chosen side, clipped to the grid. The copy may overwrite cells where the erased marker was. All eight marker orientations of both kinds are handled the same way, with no lookup table.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: exactly one marker in colour palette[6] (a T or an asymmetric cross with one unique long arm), and every palette[4] cell belongs to the figure. The copy is clipped to the grid, although the constructor guarantees it always fits. If there is no marker, the input is returned with nothing done; if there is no figure, it is returned with only the marker erased. The program does not use the demonstrations, since the handedness of the arm-to-mirror relation is fixed by d4. Not tested: I have not run this code. Constructor notes: the four unattested orientations (T stem left/right, cross long up/down) are a synthetic extension by rotation in the constructor, not something the fixtures show. The archived solver's table-plus-rot90 lookup gives the same result for rotations. I found no fixture that contradicts the uniform rule.
